note: Every number here was checked against the organization's own website or a government health site on lastVerified. Each resource lists the pages it was checked on (sources), and each region lists all of them. A wrong crisis number is worse than none: if a number can't be confirmed when re-verifying, remove it.

resources.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
resources.description: For anyone in emotional distress or thinking about suicide, or worried about someone. Also by chat at 988lifeline.org.

resources.name: National Maternal Mental Health Hotline
resources.description: Free, confidential support from trained counselors, before, during and after pregnancy. Call or text 1-833-TLC-MAMA. Interpreters in 60 languages.

resources.name: Postpartum Support International HelpLine
resources.description: Not a crisis line. Leave a message and a trained volunteer calls or texts you back with support and local resources. For any parent or family member, during pregnancy and after. En español: text 971-203-7773.

resources.name: 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline
resources.description: For anyone thinking about suicide, or worried about someone. In Quebec, calls and texts go to Quebec's own suicide prevention line.

resources.name: Hope for Wellness Help Line
resources.description: Counselling and crisis support for First Nations, Inuit and Métis people anywhere in Canada. Also by online chat.

resources.name: 1 866 APPELLE (Quebec suicide prevention)
resources.description: For anyone in Quebec thinking about suicide, worried about someone, or grieving a suicide. Text 535353, or chat at suicide.ca.

resources.name: Info-Social 811 (option 2)
resources.description: Talk to a psychosocial worker about stress, how you're feeling or a mental health worry, for yourself or someone close. Dial 811, then option 2.

resources.name: Info-Santé 811 (option 1)
resources.description: Talk to a nurse about a health question for you or your baby. Dial 811, then option 1; there's a priority line for parents of children 0 to 17. Not available in Nunavik or the Cree Territory of James Bay.

resources.name: Health811
resources.description: Free health advice from a registered nurse, and help finding local services, including mental health support. TTY: 711. Translation support in other languages.

resources.name: HealthLink BC 8-1-1
resources.description: Health service navigators and registered nurses around the clock, pharmacists overnight. Translation in over 130 languages.

resources.name: Pacific Post Partum Support Society
resources.description: Not a crisis line. Phone and text support for parents having a hard time after a baby. If you reach voicemail, leave a message with how to reach you.
resources.hours: Phone weekdays 10 am–3 pm, text 10:30 am–2:30 pm (Pacific Time)

resources.name: Health Link 811
resources.description: Health advice from a registered nurse. Support in more than 240 languages.

resources.name: HealthLine 811
resources.description: Health, mental health and addictions advice from registered nurses, psychiatric nurses and social workers. Translation in over 100 languages.

resources.name: Health Links – Info Santé
resources.description: Manitoba's health information line, toll-free anywhere in the province.

resources.name: Tele-Care 811
resources.description: Free, bilingual, confidential health line. Every caller can speak to a registered nurse.

resources.name: 811 Nova Scotia
resources.description: Talk to a registered nurse. Service in over 120 languages. If 811 doesn't connect, call 1-866-770-7763.

resources.name: 811 PEI
resources.description: Talk to a registered nurse about a health concern or question. A bilingual nurse is available in French, and interpretation in over 100 languages.

resources.name: HealthLine 811
resources.description: Nurses who listen, support you and connect you to local health services, including in a mental health or addictions crisis. If 811 doesn't connect, call 1-888-709-2929.

resources.name: NWT 811 Health Advice Line
resources.description: Confidential advice and support from registered nurses. Interpretation for French, NWT Indigenous languages and over 200 others. Toll-free: 1-844-259-1793.

resources.name: Yukon HealthLine 811
resources.description: Free, confidential health advice from a registered nurse, who can also point you to help in your community.

resources.name: Nunavut Kamatsiaqtut Help Line
resources.description: Someone to talk to, anonymously, for anyone in Nunavut. Toll-free outside Iqaluit; in Iqaluit, call 867-979-3333.

resources.name: Samaritans
resources.description: Someone to talk to, whatever you're going through. Free from any phone. Welsh language line: 0808 164 0123.

resources.name: Shout
resources.description: Free, confidential text support with a trained volunteer.

resources.name: PANDAS Foundation
resources.description: Not a crisis line. Support for parents and families with mental health difficulties in pregnancy and after. Book a free support call on their website.

resources.name: NHS 111
resources.description: Urgent health advice when it's not an emergency. In England, choose the mental health option for urgent mental health help.

resources.name: Samaritans
resources.description: Someone to talk to, whatever you're going through. Freephone.

resources.name: Text About It
resources.description: Free, anonymous text chat with a trained volunteer.

resources.name: Pieta
resources.description: Support for anyone thinking about suicide or self-harm. Freephone; standard text rates apply.

resources.name: HSE Your Mental Health information line
resources.description: Not a counselling line: tells you what mental health supports are available to you and how to get them. Freephone.

resources.name: Parentline
resources.description: Confidential support for parents, on any parenting worry.
resources.hours: Mon–Thu 10 am–9 pm, Fri 10 am–7 pm

resources.name: Aware Support Line
resources.description: Not a crisis line. Free, confidential support and information about depression, anxiety or bipolar disorder, for you or someone you care about. Also by email: Support Mail on their website.

resources.name: Cuidiú
resources.description: Not a crisis line. Volunteer breastfeeding counsellors and parent support groups around Ireland. Find your local counsellor's number on their website; if they can't answer, leave a message and they'll call you back.

resources.name: Lifeline
resources.description: Crisis support for anyone having a hard time or thinking about suicide. Also by chat at lifeline.org.au.

resources.name: PANDA National Perinatal Mental Health Helpline
resources.description: Not a crisis line. Support for expecting and new parents, through pregnancy and the first year with a baby. Open public holidays except Christmas Day.
resources.hours: Mon–Fri 9 am–7:30 pm, Sat 9 am–4 pm (AEST/AEDT)

resources.name: Pregnancy, Birth and Baby
resources.description: Talk to a maternal child health nurse. A free Australian Government service.

resources.name: healthdirect
resources.description: Health advice from a nurse or doctor, to help you know what to do. In Queensland, call 13 HEALTH instead.

resources.name: 13 HEALTH (Queensland)
resources.description: Health advice from a registered nurse in Queensland, for the cost of a local call. Child health nurses 6:30 am–11 pm.

resources.name: 1737, Need to talk?
resources.description: Free, confidential support from trained counsellors and peer support workers, for anyone in New Zealand.

resources.name: Lifeline Aotearoa
resources.description: Someone to talk to, from trained staff and volunteers. Call 0800 LIFELINE, or text HELP (4357). Not open midnight to 7 am; call or text 1737 then.

resources.name: Suicide Crisis Helpline
resources.description: For anyone thinking about suicide. Free, nationwide: 0508 TAUTOKO. Not open midnight to 7 am; call or text 1737 then.

resources.name: PlunketLine
resources.description: Parenting and child health advice from a registered Plunket nurse, free for every family. Ask for an interpreter if you need one.

resources.name: Healthline
resources.description: Free health advice any time of the day or night. Interpreters for up to 150 languages.

resources.name: ERAN, emotional first aid
resources.description: Someone to talk to, for anyone in distress. Help for new immigrants in English, Russian, French, Spanish and Amharic, Sunday to Thursday, 4–9 pm. Chat and WhatsApp on their website.

resources.name: 3114, suicide prevention
resources.description: Free national line answered by health professionals trained in suicide prevention, for anyone in distress or worried about someone.

resources.name: SOS Amitié
resources.description: Someone to listen, for anyone in distress and the people close to them. Free and anonymous, from trained volunteers. Chat every day 1 pm–3 am on their website. In English: 01 46 21 46 46, 3–11 pm.

resources.name: Allô Parents Bébé
resources.description: Free, anonymous listening and support for parents, from pregnancy until a child is 3. Run by Enfance & Partage.

resources.name: TelefonSeelsorge
resources.description: Free, anonymous support day and night, by phone, chat or email. Also on 0800 111 0 222 and 116 123.

resources.name: Ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst 116117
resources.description: Out-of-hours medical help when your doctor's office is closed. Free with a German phone contract.

resources.name: Elterntelefon (Nummer gegen Kummer)
resources.description: Free, anonymous advice for parents and other caregivers.
resources.hours: Mon, Wed, Fri 9 am–5 pm; Tue, Thu 9 am–7 pm

resources.name: 113 Zelfmoordpreventie
resources.description: Anonymous support if you're thinking about suicide. 0800-0113 is free; you can also call 113 at your usual call cost, or chat on 113.nl.

resources.name: De Luisterlijn
resources.description: Someone to talk to, day and night.

resources.name: Tele-MANAS
resources.description: Free government mental health helpline: counselling, and referral to care, including urgent care. Choose your language when you call.

resources.name: SADAG Suicide Crisis Helpline
resources.description: Toll-free crisis support from the South African Depression and Anxiety Group.

resources.name: Cipla Mental Health Helpline (SADAG)
resources.description: Toll-free mental health support from SADAG. You can also send an SMS to 31393.

resources.name: Línea 024, suicide prevention
resources.description: Free, confidential national line from the Ministry of Health, for anyone thinking about suicide and the people close to them. Also by chat, and in sign language by video, on their website.

resources.name: Telefono Amico Italia
resources.description: Someone to listen, for anyone going through an emotional crisis. Also on WhatsApp at 324 011 7252, every day 6–9 pm.

resources.name: Línea de la Vida
resources.description: Free support from a mental health professional, for suicidal thoughts, addictions, violence or any mental health worry. Run by the national mental health commission (CONASAMA).

resources.name: CVV, Centro de Valorização da Vida
resources.description: Free emotional support and suicide prevention from trained volunteers, anywhere in Brazil. Also by chat and email on their website.

resources.name: Zelfmoordlijn 1813
resources.description: Free, anonymous support for anyone thinking about suicide, or worried about someone. Chat every day 5 pm–midnight (from noon on Wednesdays).

resources.name: Centre de Prévention du Suicide
resources.description: A listening line for anyone thinking about suicide, or worried about someone.

resources.name: Die Dargebotene Hand / La Main Tendue / Telefono Amico
resources.description: Someone to talk to, personally, anonymously and confidentially. A call costs up to CHF 0.20. Also by chat and email on their website. In English: 0800 143 000, 6–11 pm.

resources.name: Självmordslinjen (Mind)
resources.description: Support for anyone thinking about suicide or in a mental health crisis, and the people close to them. Also by chat at mind.se.

resources.name: Föräldralinjen (Mind)
resources.description: Not a crisis line. Someone to talk to about being a parent and anything that worries you.
resources.hours: Weekdays 10 am–3 pm, Thursdays also 7–9 pm

resources.description: Health advice by phone, day and night.

resources.name: Mental Helse Hjelpetelefonen
resources.description: Free, anonymous line for anyone who needs someone to talk to, answered by staff and volunteers.

resources.name: Kirkens SOS
resources.description: Someone to talk to in a crisis, every day and night, holidays too. Also by chat at soschat.no.

resources.name: Legevakt (out-of-hours medical centre)
resources.description: When it's urgent but not life or death.

resources.name: Livslinien
resources.description: Anonymous support for anyone thinking about suicide, or worried about someone. Chat on weekdays 5–9 pm and weekends 1–5 pm.

resources.name: Samaritans of Singapore (SOS)
resources.description: Support for anyone in crisis, thinking about suicide, or worried about someone. Also by WhatsApp with CareText: 9151 1767.

resources.name: 18111 Mental Health Support Hotline
resources.description: The government's one-stop line for mental health support and referral, for anyone in Hong Kong. Also on WhatsApp at 18111.

resources.name: The Samaritans
resources.description: Multilingual suicide prevention hotline.

resources.name: The Samaritan Befrienders Hong Kong
resources.description: Emotional support hotline. English line: 2389 2223.

resources.name: Yorisoi Hotline (よりそいホットライン)
resources.description: Free support for any worry, from anyone, at any time. From Fukushima Prefecture: 0120-279-226. From an IP phone: 050-3655-0279.

resources.name: Inochi no Denwa (いのちの電話)
resources.description: Free line every day 4–9 pm, and from 8 am on the 10th of each month for 24 hours. Navi Dial 0570-783-556 is open 10 am–10 pm (call charges apply).

resources.name: Find A Helpline
resources.description: A free directory of helplines in over 175 countries, kept up to date daily. Find phone, text or chat support near you.
